title: openai/skills — Skills Catalog for Codex
content:
Important
This repository is deprecated. For current Codex skill and plugin examples, use the OpenAI Plugins repository. If you want to add your own skills to Codex, follow the Build plugins guide, which includes instructions for creating a skill-only plugin.
Agent Skills are folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that AI agents can discover and use to perform at specific tasks. Write once, use everywhere.
Codex uses skills to help package capabilities that teams and individuals can use to complete specific tasks in a repeatable way. This repository catalogs skills for use and distribution with Codex.
Learn more:
Skills in .system are automatically installed in the latest version of Codex.
To install curated or experimental skills, you can use the $skill-installer inside Codex.
Curated skills can be installed by name (defaults to skills/.curated):
$skill-installer gh-address-comments
For experimental skills, specify the skill folder. For example:
$skill-installer install the create-plan skill from the .experimental folder
Or provide the GitHub directory URL:
$skill-installer install https://github.com/openai/skills/tree/main/skills/.experimental/create-plan
After installing a skill, restart Codex to pick up new skills.
The license of an individual skill can be found directly inside the skill's directory inside the LICENSE.txt file.

report.summary: OpenAI's Codex skills catalog is deprecated, redirecting users to the OpenAI Plugins repository for current examples and guidance.
report.background: Agent Skills are structured folders containing instructions, scripts, and resources that AI agents can discover and use to complete tasks in a repeatable way. OpenAI introduced this format to help teams package capabilities for Codex, their agentic coding tool. The openai/skills repository served as a central catalog for curated and experimental skills, including auto-installed skills in .system and installable ones via a $skill-installer command. However, OpenAI has now deprecated this repository, consolidating skill and plugin examples under the broader OpenAI Plugins repository. This aligns with a larger shift toward unified plugin architectures, rather than having separate skill-specific catalogs. Users are encouraged to follow the Build plugins guide to create skill-only plugins, signaling that agent capabilities are maturing into a more standardized, extensible ecosystem. The concept of skills—write once, use everywhere—remains central, but its distribution and lifecycle are now governed by the plugins framework.
key_points: The repository is officially deprecated: The openai/skills repo is no longer maintained. Developers are directed to the OpenAI Plugins repository for the latest Codex skill and plugin examples. Any new additions or updates should follow the Build plugins guide instead of relying on this older catalog.

Skills are reusable agent capabilities: A skill is a folder of instructions, scripts, and resources that AI agents can discover and apply to specific tasks. This ‘write once, use everywhere’ design lets teams package repeatable workflows so Codex can invoke them consistently across projects.

Installation happens through Codex’s $skill-installer: Curated skills can be installed by name, such as gh-address-comments, while experimental skills require specifying a folder path or GitHub directory URL. After installation, users must restart Codex for new skills to be recognized.

Two skill tiers exist: Curated skills are vetted defaults stored in skills/.curated, while experimental skills live in skills/.experimental. Each skill directory carries its own LICENSE.txt, meaning usage rights vary per skill and must be checked individually before adoption.

Migration path is clear: Existing users should move to the OpenAI Plugins repository and review the skill-only plugin creation guide. This ensures compatibility with current Codex versions and avoids relying on examples from a deprecated repository.
report.impact: For AI developers, this deprecation signals that agent capability packaging is evolving from ad-hoc skill folders into a more formal plugin ecosystem. Teams who built workflows around the openai/skills catalog should migrate to the Plugins repository and the Build plugins guide to avoid breakage. For regular Codex users, most curated skills likely remain available through auto-install in .system; still, community-created skills may shift in availability. The broader AI industry will watch how OpenAI standardizes agent tooling—consolidating skills under plugins reduces fragmentation, making it easier to share and maintain agent capabilities. This transition reflects a maturing market where extensibility and modular workflows become core product differentiators, not afterthoughts.
report.tools: Watch the OpenAI Plugins repository for current skill and plugin examples. If you want to build your own, follow the Build plugins guide, which includes instructions for creating a skill-only plugin. Within Codex, use the built-in $skill-installer to experiment with curated or experimental skills, and check each skill’s LICENSE.txt before reuse.
